fullDescription: A mobile e-commerce product detail page for a fashion boutique where the size guide is drawn to scale. Instead of a row of size pills, every size plots its real garment waist measurement as a solid ink bar on one shared cm axis at a stated 10px per cm, your own measurement runs as a crosshair through every lane, the recommended size sits on an ivory card with the ease measured and printed, and the out-of-stock size gets no bar at all, just a loud diagonal hatch. Dusty rose ground, warm ivory cards, espresso ink, Cormorant Garamond serif with Karla labels, and a fashion-plate line drawing of the product. Reusable for any apparel, footwear, ring-size or fit-sensitive product page where "will it fit" should be shown rather than guessed.
prompt: {"summary": "A mobile (390px) E-COMMERCE PRODUCT DETAIL PAGE for a fashion boutique whose organising idea is a TO-SCALE FIT BOARD that IS the size selector, at a stated, checkable scale: 10px = 1 cm. Set `--cm: 10px` and derive every drawn width with `calc(var(--cm) * N)` so the drawing cannot drift from the data. NO hero headline announcing the idea, NO size-pill row, NO gradient bands, NO dot-grid textures. Page order: (1) a quiet top bar \u2014 back arrow (inline SVG), a letter-spaced serif wordmark 'MAISON RIVE', a bag icon (inline SVG); (2) a large warm-ivory product-art card holding an elegant single-weight ink LINE DRAWING of the garment (a wide-leg trouser drawn fashion-plate style in 1px strokes) with one small dusty-rose botanical sprig in the top-right corner \u2014 no photos; (3) a title block on the rose ground: a tracked serif eyebrow 'LINEN \u00b7 EDITION 04', the garment name 'The Sculpted Trouser' in Cormorant Garamond ~34px ivory, and a large serif ivory price '$148'; (4) THE FIT BOARD, labelled 'FIT, DRAWN TO SCALE' over a smaller 'WAIST, MEASURED FLAT, IN CM', with a scale key at the right: '1 CM = 10 PX' beside a hairline rule exactly calc(var(--cm) * 10) wide. The board: a hairline axis track calc(var(--cm) * 24) wide spanning 60 to 84 cm, ticks every 2 cm, numerals every 4 cm; five size rows (44px tall), each drawing a SOLID 36px-tall espresso-ink bar from the 60 cm origin to its true garment measurement \u2014 XS 64 (bar calc(var(--cm)*4)), S 68 (*8), M 72 (*12), L 76 (*16), XL 80; each bar prints its cm value at its end cap. A vertical 1px ink crosshair crosses every lane at exactly 70 cm, carrying a small 'YOUR 70 CM' flag on a ground-coloured patch. XS and S render at 40% opacity (smaller than your measurement, too tight). M is the recommended row: it sits on a full-bleed warm-ivory card, its bar carries an ivory leader from the 70 cm line to its end cap, and an ink chip prints '+2 CM EASE'. XL is OUT OF STOCK: it gets NO bar \u2014 its full lane fills with a loud 45-degree ink-on-rose diagonal hatch (bolder than any real bar) with a centred 'OUT OF STOCK' label on a ground-coloured patch. Hiding the size costs it its bar and makes it the roughest mark on the board; (5) a warm-ivory details card of two-column rows with hairline separators: FABRIC / 100% European linen, CARE / Cold wash, line dry, SHIPPING / Free over $120 \u2014 labels in tracked caps ink, values right-aligned in muted taupe; (6) one line '128 REVIEWS \u00b7 74% SAY TRUE TO SIZE' over a 2px track whose ink fill is literally 74% wide; (7) a full-width in-flow espresso-ink bar (never position:fixed) with ivory serif text 'ADD TO BAG \u00b7 SIZE M \u00b7 $148'. One currency, one price ($148 everywhere), the board's sizes and the CTA's size M agree, and 70 + 2 = 72 holds. Every number on the screen must agree with every other number.", "style": {"description": "Boutique-serif fashion register on a mid-tone dusty-rose ground \u2014 a delicate print-shop palette put to work as an instrument. Ground #c98b93 (the whole page lives on it), warm ivory #faf3f0 cards, blush #f5e8e6 secondary surface, espresso near-black #2e2224 for every load-bearing mark (bars, big type, crosshair, hatch, CTA), muted taupe #7a6a68 strictly for metadata on ivory. Measured value contrast: ink on ground 5.5:1, ivory on ground 2.8:1, ink on ivory 12.8:1 \u2014 three separated luminance bands so the board holds at squint distance and in grayscale. Display type is Cormorant Garamond (500/600), letter-spaced on eyebrows and the wordmark, generous at the title and price; all data labels, axis numerals and tracked caps are Karla at 9 to 12px. The axis track and rules are hairlines; only the bars, the type, the hatch and the CTA carry ink mass \u2014 the track never out-inks the marks it measures. Absolutely no gradients, no glows, no dot-grid or line-grid textures, no purple or indigo, no emoji, no photos. Pure HTML and CSS (Tailwind ok), no JavaScript, self-contained in one file with Google Fonts via link tag.", "fonts": "Cormorant Garamond (Google Fonts) 500/600 for wordmark, eyebrow, title, price and CTA; Karla 400/500 for axis numerals, size letters, row labels, detail rows and all tracked-caps metadata.", "colors": "ground #c98b93, card #faf3f0, secondary surface #f5e8e6, ink #2e2224, muted #7a6a68"}, "layout_and_structure": "Mobile-first single column at 390px, fluid \u2014 never a fixed-width container, never h-screen or overflow:hidden on the page shell, so the page scrolls at its natural height. At md+ it becomes a two-pane split: the product-art card in a sticky left pane (md:w-1/2 md:h-screen md:sticky md:top-0), title/fit-board/details/CTA in the right pane. On mobile, cap the art card so the fit board's label and first rows enter the first viewport (svg max-h around 36vh) \u2014 the mechanic must be visible on the first screen, not announced by a headline. The fit board is one position:relative container: a hairline track div (width calc(var(--cm) * 24), margin-left matching the 32px size-letter gutter) carrying absolutely-positioned ticks and numerals at left calc(var(--cm) * N); the crosshair is an absolutely positioned 1px ink div at left calc(32px + var(--cm) * 10) spanning the container's height; each size row is a 44px flex row of a 32px size-letter span, the drawn bar div at width calc(var(--cm) * N), and the cm numeral. The recommended row is wrapped in a -mx-3 px-3 ivory card so its bar stays origin-aligned with every other row (verify by DOM probe: all bar lefts equal, bar widths exactly 40/80/120/160/200px, crosshair at origin + 100px). The 10px-per-cm rule is the whole layout system \u2014 if a measurement changes, only the N in the calc() changes.", "special_ui_components": [{"component": "To-scale fit board", "description": "The core mechanic. A shared horizontal cm axis where 10px = 1 cm, so every size's bar length IS its real garment measurement and 'which size' becomes a chart you read instead of a guess. An on-screen scale key makes the claim checkable.", "prompt": "Build a position:relative board. Draw a 1px hairline track of width calc(var(--cm) * 24) (with --cm: 10px) offset by a 32px left gutter, spanning 60 to 84 cm: absolutely position 2cm minor ticks and 4cm major ticks with numerals at left calc(var(--cm) * N). Below it, stack five 44px-tall flex rows, one per size: a 32px size-letter span (Karla), then a solid espresso-ink bar div of height 36px and width calc(var(--cm) * (measurement - 60)) \u2014 XS 64cm = *4, S 68 = *8, M 72 = *12, L 76 = *16, XL 80 = *20 \u2014 then the cm value printed at the end cap. Rows smaller than the shopper's measurement render at 40% opacity (too tight). Add a scale key in the board header: the text '1 CM = 10 PX' beside a hairline rule of width exactly calc(var(--cm) * 10). The track and ticks stay hairlines; only the bars carry mass."}, {"component": "Your-measurement crosshair with ease leader", "description": "A vertical 1px line at the shopper's own measurement crossing every lane, and on the recommended row a leader from the line to the bar's end cap printing the ease in cm \u2014 fit shown as measurable geometry.", "prompt": "Absolutely position a 1px espresso-ink vertical line at left calc(32px + var(--cm) * 10) (the shopper's 70 cm) spanning the board's full height, z-index above the bars, with a small 'YOUR 70 CM' flag in 9px bold tracked Karla on a ground-coloured patch at its top. Wrap the recommended row (M, 72 cm) in a full-bleed warm-ivory card (-mx-3 px-3 so the bar stays origin-aligned). Inside M's bar, draw a 1px ivory leader from left calc(var(--cm) * 10) spanning calc(var(--cm) * 2) \u2014 the 70-to-72 gap \u2014 and just past the end cap place an ink chip with ivory 8px bold text reading '+2 CM EASE'. The arithmetic must hold: your measurement + printed ease = the row's cm value."}, {"component": "Hatched out-of-stock lane", "description": "The unavailable size loses its bar entirely: its lane fills with a loud 45-degree diagonal hatch, deliberately drawn bolder than any real bar, with an OUT OF STOCK label breaking it on a ground patch.", "prompt": "For the out-of-stock size, render NO solid bar. Fill its lane (height 36px, width calc(var(--cm) * 20)) with background: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, #2e2224, #2e2224 2px, transparent 2px, transparent 8px). Centre a label over it: 'OUT OF STOCK' in 9px bold tracked Karla on a solid ground-coloured (#c98b93) patch so it stays legible. Dim the row's size letter and cm numeral to 60%. The hatch must read as the roughest, loudest mark on the board \u2014 absence drawn louder than presence."}, {"component": "Fashion-plate product card", "description": "A warm-ivory card holding a single-weight ink line drawing of the garment instead of a photo, with one small dusty-rose botanical sprig \u2014 the product rendered in the same drawn language as the fit board.", "prompt": "Compose a large warm-ivory (#faf3f0) card holding an inline SVG line drawing of the garment: 1px espresso-ink strokes, stroke-linecap round, fashion-plate style (waistband, legs, a centre seam, two lighter 0.5px fold lines at 60% opacity), fill none, viewBox sized to the garment. Add one small dusty-rose (#c98b93) botanical sprig SVG in the top-right corner \u2014 fine stems with small filled dots, never overlapping the garment. On mobile cap the drawing around max-h 36vh so the content below enters the first screen; on desktop let the card fill a sticky left pane. No photos, no mockups, no gradients."}]}
